questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the elementary termolecular gas-phase reaction $2\text{NO}(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \to 2\text{NO}_2(g)$, which statement is strictly TRUE regarding its rate law and molecularity?
optionsEn: The reaction order is $2$ and molecularity is $3$.
The reaction order can be fractional, whereas molecularity is $2$.
Both the overall reaction order and molecularity are equal to $3$.
The rate constant has SI units of $\text{m}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1}$.
questions.explanationEn: For a single-step elementary reaction, the reaction order with respect to each reactant equals its stoichiometric coefficient. Here the elementary step involves $2$ molecules of $\text{NO}$ and $1$ molecule of $\text{O}_2$, so both the molecularity and the overall order equal $2 + 1 = 3$. For a third-order reaction, the SI unit of $k$ is $\text{m}^6\text{ mol}^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A reactant $\text{X}$ decomposes via two parallel first-order channels: $\text{X} \xrightarrow{k_1} \text{Y}$ (activation energy $E_1$) and $\text{X} \xrightarrow{k_2} \text{Z}$ (activation energy $E_2$). The apparent overall activation energy $E_{\text{app}}$ for the disappearance of $\text{X}$ is
questions.explanationEn: The overall rate constant for the disappearance of $\text{X}$ is $k_{\text{obs}} = k_1 + k_2$. By definition, $E_{\text{app}} = RT^2 \frac{d\ln k_{\text{obs}}}{dT} = \frac{RT^2}{k_1 + k_2}\left(\frac{dk_1}{dT} + \frac{dk_2}{dT}\right)$. Since $RT^2 \frac{dk_i}{dT} = k_i E_i$, we obtain $E_{\text{app}} = \frac{k_1 E_1 + k_2 E_2}{k_1 + k_2}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The photochemical reaction $\text{H}_2(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g) \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{HCl}(g)$ exhibits a quantum yield $\Phi$ on the order of $10^4$ to $10^6$ because
optionsEn: absorption of a single photon initiates a self-sustaining free-radical chain propagation cycle
the Einstein of radiation supplies enough energy to dissociate $10^5$ molecules of $\text{Cl}_2$ simultaneously
the primary photochemical step violates the Stark-Einstein law of photochemical equivalence
each excited $\text{Cl}_2^*$ molecule undergoes phosphorescence before reacting
questions.explanationEn: The Stark-Einstein law applies strictly to the primary absorption step (one photon excites one $\text{Cl}_2$ molecule to form two $\text{Cl}^\bullet$ radicals). However, each $\text{Cl}^\bullet$ radical participates in thousands of secondary chain-propagation cycles ($\text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{H}_2 \to \text{HCl} + \text{H}^\bullet$ and $\text{H}^\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \to \text{HCl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$) before termination, resulting in an overall quantum yield $\Phi \gg 1$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A diatomic gas $\text{X}_2$ undergoes dissociative chemisorption on a solid surface as $\text{X}_2(g) + 2\text{S} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{X-S}$ with equilibrium constant $K$. According to the Langmuir model, the fractional surface coverage $\theta$ at pressure $P$ is given by
questions.explanationEn: For dissociative adsorption requiring two adjacent vacant sites, the rate of adsorption is $r_a = k_a P (1 - \theta)^2$ and the rate of associative desorption is $r_d = k_d \theta^2$. At equilibrium ($r_a = r_d$), $\frac{\theta^2}{(1 - \theta)^2} = \frac{k_a}{k_d} P = KP \implies \frac{\theta}{1 - \theta} = (KP)^{1/2}$. Solving for $\theta$ gives $\theta = \frac{(KP)^{1/2}}{1 + (KP)^{1/2}}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a polydisperse synthetic polymer sample obeying the Mark-Houwink equation with exponent $a = 0.70$, the correct ordering of the number-average ($M_n$), viscosity-average ($M_v$), weight-average ($M_w$), and z-average ($M_z$) molar masses is
questions.explanationEn: For any polydisperse polymer, higher moments weight heavier chains more strongly, giving $M_n < M_w < M_z$. The viscosity-average molar mass is $M_v = \left(\frac{\sum N_i M_i^{1+a}}{\sum N_i M_i}\right)^{1/a}$. Since typical flexible polymers have $0.5 \le a \le 0.8$ (here $0 < a = 0.70 < 1$), $M_v$ lies strictly between $M_n$ and $M_w$ (and equals $M_w$ when $a = 1$). Thus, $M_n < M_v < M_w < M_z$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an $n$th-order reaction $\text{A} \to \text{Products}$ with rate law $-\frac{d[\text{A}]}{dt} = k[\text{A}]^n$ (where $n > 0$ and $n \neq 1$), the CORRECT statement(s) is(are)
optionsEn: A plot of $\ln[\text{A}]$ versus $t$ is strictly linear for all values of $n$.
The units of the rate constant $k$ are $(\text{mol L}^{-1})^{1-n}\text{ s}^{-1}$.
questions.explanationEn: Integrating $-\frac{d[\text{A}]}{[\text{A}]^n} = k\,dt$ for $n \neq 1$ yields $\frac{1}{[\text{A}]^{n-1}} - \frac{1}{[\text{A}]_0^{n-1}} = (n-1)kt$ (C is true). Setting $[\text{A}] = [\text{A}]_0/2$ gives $t_{1/2} = \frac{2^{n-1}-1}{(n-1)k[\text{A}]_0^{n-1}} \propto [\text{A}]_0^{1-n}$ (A is true). From $\text{rate} = k[\text{A}]^n$, $k$ has units $(\text{mol L}^{-1})^{1-n}\text{ s}^{-1}$ (D is true). A linear plot of $\ln[\text{A}]$ vs $t$ holds only for $n = 1$ (B is false). Thus, (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following are fundamental assumptions of the classical Langmuir adsorption isotherm?
optionsEn: All adsorption sites on the solid surface are energetically equivalent.
Adsorbed molecules form an unlimited number of stacked layers at high pressure.
There are no lateral interactions between molecules adsorbed on neighboring sites.
Each surface site can accommodate at most one adsorbed species.
questions.explanationEn: The Langmuir model assumes a uniform surface of energetically identical sites (A), localized monolayer adsorption with at most one adsorbate per site (D), and zero lateral adsorbate-adsorbate interactions so that $\Delta H_{\text{ads}}$ is independent of coverage (C). Multilayer adsorption is described by the BET isotherm, not Langmuir (B is false). Thus, (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A first-order decomposition reaction $\text{A} \to \text{Products}$ has a half-life of $16\text{ min}$ at $310\text{ K}$. The time (in $\text{min}$) required for $87.5\%$ of $\text{A}$ to decompose at the same temperature is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For a first-order reaction, the half-life $t_{1/2} = 16\text{ min}$ is independent of concentration. When $87.5\%$ of $\text{A}$ has decomposed, the remaining fraction is $1 - 0.875 = 0.125 = \frac{1}{8} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3$, which corresponds to exactly $3$ half-lives. Therefore, $t = 3 \times 16\text{ min} = 48\text{ min}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the reversible first-order isomerization $\text{A} \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{B}$, the forward rate constant is $k_1 = 0.04\text{ s}^{-1}$ and the equilibrium constant is $K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{[\text{B}]_{\text{eq}}}{[\text{A}]_{\text{eq}}} = 4.0$. The relaxation time $\tau$ (in $\text{s}$) of the system is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: At equilibrium, $K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{k_1}{k_{-1}}$, so the reverse rate constant is $k_{-1} = \frac{k_1}{K_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{0.04}{4.0} = 0.01\text{ s}^{-1}$. The relaxation time for a first-order reversible reaction is $\tau = \frac{1}{k_1 + k_{-1}} = \frac{1}{0.04 + 0.01} = \frac{1}{0.05} = 20\text{ s}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A polymer blend is prepared by mixing $0.20\text{ mol}$ of monodisperse chains of molar mass $10\text{ kg mol}^{-1}$ with $0.30\text{ mol}$ of monodisperse chains of molar mass $30\text{ kg mol}^{-1}$. The number-average molar mass $M_n$ (in $\text{kg mol}^{-1}$) of the blend is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: The number-average molar mass is defined as $M_n = \frac{\sum n_i M_i}{\sum n_i}$. Substituting the given moles and molar masses gives $M_n = \frac{(0.20 \times 10) + (0.30 \times 30)}{0.20 + 0.30} = \frac{2.0 + 9.0}{0.50} = \frac{11.0}{0.50} = 22\text{ kg mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following mechanism for the thermal decomposition of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$:
(i) $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5 \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{NO}_2 + \text{NO}_3$
(ii) $\text{NO}_2 + \text{NO}_3 \xrightarrow{k_2} \text{NO} + \text{O}_2 + \text{NO}_2$
(iii) $\text{NO} + \text{NO}_3 \xrightarrow{k_3} 2\text{NO}_2$
Applying the steady-state approximation to $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_3$, the rate of formation of $\text{O}_2$ is
questions.explanationEn: Applying SSA to $\text{NO}$: $\frac{d[\text{NO}]}{dt} = k_2[\text{NO}_2][\text{NO}_3] - k_3[\text{NO}][\text{NO}_3] = 0 \implies k_3[\text{NO}] = k_2[\text{NO}_2]$. Applying SSA to $\text{NO}_3$: $k_1[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5] - (k_{-1} + k_2)[\text{NO}_2][\text{NO}_3] - k_3[\text{NO}][\text{NO}_3] = 0$. Substituting $k_3[\text{NO}] = k_2[\text{NO}_2]$ gives $[\text{NO}_2][\text{NO}_3] = \frac{k_1[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]}{k_{-1} + 2k_2}$. Therefore, $\frac{d[\text{O}_2]}{dt} = k_2[\text{NO}_2][\text{NO}_3] = \frac{k_1 k_2}{k_{-1} + 2k_2}[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The gas-phase reaction $2\text{NO}(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \to 2\text{NO}_2(g)$ displays a negative apparent activation energy ($E_{\text{app}} < 0$) because it proceeds via a rapid pre-equilibrium $2\text{NO} \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_2$ ($\Delta H^\circ_{\text{eq}}$) followed by a slow step $\text{N}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{k_2} 2\text{NO}_2$ (activation energy $E_2$). This requires that
questions.explanationEn: Under the rapid pre-equilibrium approximation, the observed rate constant is $k_{\text{obs}} = K_{\text{eq}} k_2$. Using the van 't Hoff and Arrhenius relations, $E_{\text{app}} = RT^2 \frac{d\ln k_{\text{obs}}}{dT} = \Delta H^\circ_{\text{eq}} + E_2$ (for concentrations, $\Delta U^\circ_{\text{eq}} + E_2$). For $E_{\text{app}}$ to be negative, the pre-equilibrium dimerization must be exothermic ($\Delta H^\circ_{\text{eq}} < 0$) and its magnitude must exceed $E_2$ ($|\Delta H^\circ_{\text{eq}}| > E_2$). Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An excited singlet molecule $S_1$ decays via fluorescence ($k_f$), internal conversion ($k_{\text{ic}}$), and intersystem crossing ($k_{\text{isc}}$). If its measured fluorescence quantum yield is $\Phi_f = 0.25$ and its observed fluorescence lifetime is $\tau_f = 5.0\text{ ns}$, the radiative rate constant $k_f$ and natural (radiative) lifetime $\tau_0^{\text{rad}} = 1/k_f$ are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: The fluorescence quantum yield is $\Phi_f = \frac{k_f}{k_f + k_{\text{ic}} + k_{\text{isc}}} = k_f \tau_f$. Therefore, $k_f = \frac{\Phi_f}{\tau_f} = \frac{0.25}{5.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s}} = 5.0 \times 10^7\text{ s}^{-1}$. The natural radiative lifetime is $\tau_0^{\text{rad}} = \frac{1}{k_f} = \frac{1}{5.0 \times 10^7\text{ s}^{-1}} = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ s} = 20.0\text{ ns}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The isosteric enthalpy of adsorption ($\Delta_{\text{ads}} H^\circ$) of a gas on a solid surface at constant fractional coverage $\theta$ can be determined from the temperature dependence of the equilibrium pressure $P$ using the Clausius-Clapeyron-type relation
questions.explanationEn: From the Langmuir isotherm at fixed $\theta$, $KP = \frac{\theta}{1-\theta} = \text{constant}$, so $\ln K + \ln P = \text{constant}$. Differentiating with respect to $T$ at constant $\theta$ gives $\left(\frac{\partial \ln P}{\partial T}\right)_\theta = -\frac{d\ln K}{dT}$. By the van 't Hoff equation, $\frac{d\ln K}{dT} = \frac{\Delta_{\text{ads}} H^\circ}{RT^2}$, yielding $\left(\frac{\partial \ln P}{\partial T}\right)_\theta = -\frac{\Delta_{\text{ads}} H^\circ}{RT^2}$ (positive since adsorption is exothermic, $\Delta_{\text{ads}} H^\circ < 0$). Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a linear step-growth polymerization between $N_A$ moles of a diacid $\text{A-A}$ and $N_B$ moles of a diol $\text{B-B}$ with stoichiometric ratio $r = \frac{N_A}{N_B} < 1$, the maximum number-average degree of polymerization $X_n$ achievable at complete conversion of the limiting monomer ($p = 1$) is
questions.explanationEn: For step-growth polymerization with stoichiometric imbalance $r = N_A/N_B \le 1$, the generalized Carothers equation is $X_n = \frac{1 + r}{1 + r - 2rp}$. At complete conversion of the limiting A groups ($p = 1$), this simplifies to $X_n = \frac{1 + r}{1 + r - 2r} = \frac{1 + r}{1 - r}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the two-step reaction $\text{A} + \text{B} \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{I} \xrightarrow{k_2} \text{P}$, applying the steady-state approximation to intermediate $\text{I}$ gives $\frac{d[\text{P}]}{dt} = \frac{k_1 k_2 [\text{A}][\text{B}]}{k_{-1} + k_2}$. The CORRECT statement(s) is(are)
optionsEn: When $k_{-1} \gg k_2$, the rate law reduces to the pre-equilibrium expression $\frac{k_1 k_2}{k_{-1}}[\text{A}][\text{B}]$.
When $k_2 \gg k_{-1}$, the overall rate constant equals $k_2$.
When $k_2 \gg k_{-1}$, the formation of $\text{I}$ is the rate-determining step and $\frac{d[\text{P}]}{dt} = k_1[\text{A}][\text{B}]$.
In the pre-equilibrium limit ($k_{-1} \gg k_2$), the apparent activation energy is $E_1 - E_{-1} + E_2$.
questions.explanationEn: If $k_{-1} \gg k_2$, then $k_{-1} + k_2 \approx k_{-1}$, yielding $\frac{d[\text{P}]}{dt} = \frac{k_1 k_2}{k_{-1}}[\text{A}][\text{B}]$ (A is true) with $E_{\text{app}} = E_1 - E_{-1} + E_2$ (D is true). If $k_2 \gg k_{-1}$, then $k_{-1} + k_2 \approx k_2$, so $k_2$ cancels out and $\frac{d[\text{P}]}{dt} = k_1[\text{A}][\text{B}]$, making step 1 rate-determining (C is true, B is false). Thus, (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For the elementary reversible first-order reaction $\text{A} \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{B}$ starting with $[\text{A}]_0 > 0$ and $[\text{B}]_0 = 0$, the CORRECT statement(s) is(are)
optionsEn: The standard reaction enthalpy satisfies $\Delta_r H^\circ = E_{a,1} - E_{a,-1}$.
A plot of $\ln([\text{A}]_t - [\text{A}]_{\text{eq}})$ versus $t$ is a straight line with slope $-(k_1 + k_{-1})$.
questions.explanationEn: At equilibrium, $k_1[\text{A}]_{\text{eq}} = k_{-1}[\text{B}]_{\text{eq}}$ with $[\text{A}]_{\text{eq}} + [\text{B}]_{\text{eq}} = [\text{A}]_0$, giving $[\text{A}]_{\text{eq}} = \frac{k_{-1}}{k_1 + k_{-1}}[\text{A}]_0$ (A is false) and $[\text{B}]_{\text{eq}} = \frac{k_1}{k_1 + k_{-1}}[\text{A}]_0$ (B is true). Since $K_{\text{eq}} = k_1/k_{-1}$, $\Delta_r H^\circ = E_{a,1} - E_{a,-1}$ (C is true). Because $[\text{A}]_t - [\text{A}]_{\text{eq}} = ([\text{A}]_0 - [\text{A}]_{\text{eq}})e^{-(k_1+k_{-1})t}$, plotting $\ln([\text{A}]_t - [\text{A}]_{\text{eq}})$ vs $t$ gives slope $-(k_1 + k_{-1})$ (D is true). Thus, (B), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Regarding step-growth polymerization and network formation (Carothers theory of gelation), the CORRECT statement(s) is(are)
optionsEn: When a trifunctional monomer is included so that the average functionality is $f_{\text{avg}} > 2$, the critical extent of reaction at the gel point is $p_c = \frac{2}{f_{\text{avg}}}$.
In an uncatalyzed self-catalyzed polyesterification of a diacid and equimolar diol, the reaction follows overall third-order kinetics ($\frac{1}{(1-p)^2} - 1 = 2k[\text{M}]_0^2 t$).
Adding a small amount of monofunctional carboxylic acid to an equimolar diacid-diol polymerization increases the maximum attainable molar mass.
In a catalyzed polyesterification with an external strong acid, $X_n$ increases exponentially with time $t$.
questions.explanationEn: By Carothers gelation theory, $X_n = \frac{2}{2 - p f_{\text{avg}}} \to \infty$ at $p_c = \frac{2}{f_{\text{avg}}}$ (A is true). Uncatalyzed polyesterification is second-order in $-\text{COOH}$ and first-order in $-\text{OH}$ (overall 3rd order), integrating to $\frac{1}{(1-p)^2} - 1 = 2k[\text{M}]_0^2 t$ (B is true). A monofunctional acid caps chain ends and strictly lowers molar mass (C is false). External-acid-catalyzed polyesterification is second-order, giving $X_n = 1 + k'[\text{M}]_0 t$, linear in $t$ (D is false). Thus, (A) and (B) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An enzyme-catalyzed reaction obeying Michaelis-Menten kinetics is run at a substrate concentration $[\text{S}] = 2K_M$. A reversible competitive inhibitor with inhibition constant $K_I = 4.0\text{ }\mu\text{M}$ is added. The inhibitor concentration (in $\mu\text{M}$) required to reduce the initial reaction rate to exactly half of its uninhibited value is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Without inhibitor at $[\text{S}] = 2K_M$, the rate is $v_0 = \frac{v_{\max}(2K_M)}{K_M + 2K_M} = \frac{2}{3}v_{\max}$. With a competitive inhibitor, $v_I = \frac{v_{\max}(2K_M)}{K_M(1 + [\text{I}]/K_I) + 2K_M}$. Setting $v_I = \frac{1}{2}v_0 = \frac{1}{3}v_{\max}$ gives $\frac{2}{3 + [\text{I}]/K_I} = \frac{1}{3} \implies 3 + \frac{[\text{I}]}{K_I} = 6 \implies [\text{I}] = 3K_I = 3 \times 4.0\text{ }\mu\text{M} = 12\text{ }\mu\text{M}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Chemical Kinetics, Surface & Polymer Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a BET adsorption experiment, a linear plot of $\frac{z}{(1-z)V}$ versus $z = P/P^*$ yields a slope of $4.95 \times 10^{-2}\text{ cm}^{-3}$ and a $y$-intercept of $5.00 \times 10^{-4}\text{ cm}^{-3}$. The value of the dimensionless BET constant $c$ is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: In the linearized BET equation $\frac{z}{(1-z)V} = \frac{1}{cV_m} + \left(\frac{c-1}{cV_m}\right)z$, the intercept is $I = \frac{1}{cV_m}$ and the slope is $S = \frac{c-1}{cV_m}$. Dividing the slope by the intercept gives $\frac{S}{I} = c - 1 = \frac{4.95 \times 10^{-2}}{5.00 \times 10^{-4}} = 99$. Therefore, $c = 99 + 1 = 100$.
